name: SP3485EN-L_TR
title: SP3485: +3.3 V low-power half-duplex RS-485/RS-422 transceiver, 10 Mbps
summary: One driver and one receiver for RS-485 and RS-422 buses, sharing the A/B pair, powered from a single 3.3 V supply. Data runs at up to 10 Mbps in both directions, with DE (active high) and RE (active low) enables, a -7 V to +12 V bus common-mode range and a short-circuit-limited driver. It uses the 75176 pin arrangement in an 8-pin narrow SOIC and works with 5 V logic. SP3485EN-L/TR is the -40 °C to +85 °C grade on tape and reel.
key_figures: 1.5 V min into R = 27Ω (RS-485), 2 V min into R = 50Ω (RS-422)

pins.name: RO
pins.function: Receiver output: high when A - B is +0.2 V or more, low at -0.2 V or less, high with both bus inputs open; high impedance while RE is high.

pins.name: RE
pins.function: Receiver output enable, active low. Low turns RO on; high puts RO at high impedance.

pins.name: DE
pins.function: Driver output enable, active high. High lets the driver drive A and B; low leaves both at high impedance.

pins.name: DI
pins.function: Driver data input. With DE high, DI high drives A high and B low; DI low drives A low and B high.

pins.name: A
pins.function: Bus line A: the driver's non-inverting output and the receiver's non-inverting input.

pins.name: B
pins.function: Bus line B: the driver's inverting output and the receiver's inverting input.

operation.text: A 3.3 V half-duplex RS-485/RS-422 transceiver built in a BiCMOS process. Its pins match the SP481, SP483 and SP485 and the 75176 arrangement. It is interoperable with 5.0 V logic, and up to 32 such transceivers may share one bus.

A and B form a differential output meeting RS-485 and RS-422. With no load the output swing is typically 0 V to 3.3 V; with 54 Ω across the pair the differential level stays above 1.5 V. DE high turns the outputs on and DE low puts them at high impedance. The driver runs at up to 10 Mbps. Output current is held to 250 mA at most, so a short to any voltage from -7.0 V to +12 V can last indefinitely without destroying the part.

The inputs respond to ±200 mV between A and B and present 15 kΩ typical (12 kΩ minimum). Their -7 V to +12 V common-mode window tolerates large ground offsets between nodes. If the inputs are left floating, RO goes high (fail-safe). RE low turns RO on; RE high puts it at high impedance. The receiver runs at up to 10 Mbps.

Logic inputs (DI, DE, RE, and the receiver test input) step between 0 V and 3 V and are timed at 1.5 V. Driver single-ended outputs are timed at VOM, about 1.5 V; the differential output, which swings about +2.0 V to -2.0 V, is timed at 50% for delay and between 10% and 90% for rise and fall. Driver disable times end when the output has moved 0.25 V from its driven level. Receiver delays end at VCC/2; receiver disable ends after a 10% change of the output and receiver enable at an output of 1.5 V.
Pulses in the test circuits come from a 50 Ω source at 250 kHz, 50% duty, with rise time under 6.0 ns.
